dialogue.content: I spent the first hour tidying the demo script and closing stale entries.
Anything still open?
Two items, both with owners.
The prototype build review wrapped early today.
Any surprises in it?
None worth recording.
Internal design reviews, adversarial as they get, are comfortable at any depth.
Internal scrutiny is home ground.
The most useful ground there is.
Someone new shadowed me in the design studio this morning.
Did that slow you down?
A little, but the questions were good ones.
I batched my replies about the stage rehearsals into one message before lunch.
Cleaner than drip-feeding answers.
Much cleaner.
The launch keynote demo went flawlessly because we ran two full technical rehearsals; both times the rehearsal surfaced a failure we fixed before stage.
The rehearsals were where the demo was actually won.
Both wins happened before the audience existed.
Unrehearsed hallway demos of stable features are easy.
Low-stakes improvisation is fine.
Stable features improvise themselves.
I archived last cycle's notes on the prototype build and set up the new folder.
A fresh start?
As fresh as these things get.
The launch clip is still used by sales; its success has a long commercial tail.
The prepared format compounds.
Compounds quarterly, per the sales team.
A vendor call about the demo script ran long but ended well.
Worth the time?
This one, yes.
I walked through the design studio checklist with the new starter.
How did they do?
Careful and quick, a good sign.
Quiet afternoon; I cleared the backlog around the stage rehearsals.
A rare day.
I did not waste it.
I flagged a small inconsistency in the prototype build records and fixed it at the source.
Root cause or symptom?
Root cause, for once.
The design conference slot I have been offered includes two scheduled tech rehearsals and a captured backup video of the demo, the exact structure of the launch.
The offer replicates your winning structure.
Replicates it point for point.
I sketched next week's plan for the stage rehearsals before leaving.
Ahead of schedule?
Ahead enough to sleep well.
Lunch walk, then a clean pass through the demo script updates.
Does the walk help?
It resets the afternoon.
The conference audience includes three companies we are actively recruiting from.
The stakes are real and aligned.
Aligned with the structure in place.
I compared two options for the prototype build tooling and noted a mild preference.
Decision made?
Deferred until the trial ends.
I closed the week by updating the design studio handover notes.
Anything unusual to hand over?
Blessedly little.
The conference slot needs confirmation this week. Given how my demos succeed, is this the right stage for me?
